meta.name: The Lord of the Rings
meta.description: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers & The Return of the King -- J.R.R. Tolkien

vol_communaute.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
vol_communaute.description: First volume -- from the Shire to the breaking at Parth Galen.

vol_deux_tours.title: The Two Towers
vol_deux_tours.description: Second volume -- three narrative threads between Fangorn, Rohan and Mordor.

vol_retour_roi.title: The Return of the King
vol_retour_roi.description: Third volume -- siege of Gondor, destruction of the Ring, coronation and the Grey Havens.

char_frodo.name: Frodo Baggins
char_frodo.description: Adopted nephew of Bilbo Baggins and heir to Bag End. Frodo inherits the One Ring without knowing its nature. His resistance to the Ring's corruption -- partial but real -- sets him apart from every other creature in Middle-earth.

char_aragorn.name: Aragorn
char_aragorn.description: Direct heir of Isildur and thus rightful claimant to the thrones of Gondor and Arnor. He lives under the secret identity of 'Strider', a Ranger of the wild, until the Quest of the Ring reveals his destiny.
char_aragorn.role: Ranger of the North, Heir of Isildur

char_gandalf.name: Gandalf the Grey
char_gandalf.description: One of the five Istari sent by the Valar to aid the Free Peoples against Sauron. Unlike Saruman, he refuses the pursuit of power. Bearer of Narya, the Ring of Fire. His fall at Khazad-dum marks the end of Gandalf the Grey -- and the beginning of Gandalf the White.
char_gandalf.role: Wizard of the Order, Guide of the Fellowship

char_sam.name: Samwise Gamgee
char_sam.description: Devoted gardener of Bilbo, then steadfast companion of Frodo. His unwavering loyalty and deep love for Frodo will drive him to deeds of bravery that will surprise even himself. He is the true anchor of the Quest.

char_merry.name: Meriadoc Brandybuck
char_merry.description: The most intellectual and organized of the young hobbits. Merry knows the Shire like the back of his hand and can navigate the wild. His curiosity and practicality make him invaluable to the Fellowship.

char_pippin.name: Peregrin Took
char_pippin.description: The youngest and most impulsive of the hobbits. His recklessness will get him into trouble (notably with the Palantir), but his pure heart and loyalty make him a precious companion. He represents innocence confronted with the world.

char_legolas.name: Legolas
char_legolas.description: Son of King Thranduil, representative of the Elves at the Council of Elrond. An archer of superhuman precision, he sees and hears things invisible to mortals. His budding friendship with Gimli will break a millennia-old taboo between Elves and Dwarves.

char_gimli.name: Gimli
char_gimli.description: Son of Gloin (companion of Bilbo during the journey to Erebor). Representative of the Dwarves at the Council of Elrond. His legendary endurance and courage in close combat make him a pillar of the Fellowship. His friendship with Legolas will become legendary.

char_boromir.name: Boromir
char_boromir.description: Eldest son of Denethor II, Steward of Gondor. He comes to Rivendell to interpret a prophetic dream. A noble and patriotic warrior, he gradually succumbs to the allure of the Ring, which he sees as the weapon that could save his people. His final redemption remains one of the most powerful moments of the tale.

char_galadriel.name: Galadriel
char_galadriel.description: One of the oldest and most powerful Elves of Middle-earth. Bearer of Nenya, the Ring of Adamant. She has protected Lothlorien for centuries. Her refusal of the One Ring, offered by Frodo, is an act of renunciation of immense moral grandeur.
char_galadriel.role: Lady of Lothlorien, Bearer of Nenya

char_elrond.name: Elrond
char_elrond.description: Son of Earendil and Elwing, one of the oldest beings in Middle-earth. He founded Rivendell after the war of the Age of Glory. Bearer of Vilya, the Ring of Air. He presides over the Council that decides the fate of the One Ring.
char_elrond.role: Lord of Rivendell, Bearer of Vilya

char_saruman.name: Saruman the White
char_saruman.description: The head of the Order of the Istari, formerly the wisest and most powerful of the five wizards. His pursuit of knowledge about the One Ring corrupted him. He now seeks to seize the Ring for himself, betraying the Order and the Free Peoples.
char_saruman.role: Head of the Istari Order, Traitor
traits: Corrupted by the pursuit of power

char_bilbo.name: Bilbo Baggins
char_bilbo.description: Frodo's uncle and the first 'accidental' bearer of the One Ring since Gollum's disappearance. He lived extraordinarily long thanks to the Ring. At Rivendell, he works on his book 'There and Back Again' and eventually passes his memories on to Frodo.

char_glorfindel.name: Glorfindel
char_glorfindel.description: One of the Elf-lords of Rivendell. Sent by Elrond to meet the Fellowship, he saves Frodo by offering his own Elven mount, Asfaloth, to flee the Nazgul. His inner light is so powerful it can repel the Nine.

char_celeborn.name: Celeborn
char_celeborn.description: Husband of Galadriel and co-lord of Lothlorien. An accomplished warrior and strategist, less versed in mystical arts than his wife but of equal wisdom in the affairs of the world. He welcomes the Fellowship with justified wariness, tempered by love for his wife.

char_tom_bombadil.name: Tom Bombadil
char_tom_bombadil.description: A mysterious being whose true nature is not explained, not even by Tolkien. He is the 'Master' of the Old Forest and the Barrow-downs. The One Ring has no power over him -- he can make it disappear and reappear as though it were a common pebble.

char_gwaihir.name: Gwaihir
char_gwaihir.description: The greatest and wisest of the Eagles, descendant of Thorondor. He answers Gandalf's call and rescues him from Isengard. His aid will prove decisive at several critical moments of the War of the Ring. Swift as the wind, he can cover enormous distances.
char_gwaihir.role: Lord of the Eagles, Ally of Gandalf

char_gollum.name: Gollum
char_gollum.description: Once Smeagol, a Stoor-hobbit of the Gladden Fields. The Ring corrupted him over five hundred years, transforming him into a tortured creature divided between his remaining humanity (Smeagol) and the voice of obsession (Gollum). He knows the road to Mordor better than anyone.

char_theoden.name: Theoden
char_theoden.description: King of Rohan, paralyzed by the sorcery of Grima Wormtongue -- Saruman's agent. Freed by Gandalf the White, he is reborn as a war leader and leads his people to the Battle of Helm's Deep. His death on the Pelennor Fields will be one of the most celebrated heroic acts of the War.

char_eomer.name: Eomer
char_eomer.description: Nephew of Theoden and future king of Rohan. An impetuous and loyal warrior, he makes independent decisions when honor demands it -- which earns him temporary banishment by Theoden under Grima's influence. His light cavalry will be decisive in several battles.

char_eowyn.name: Eowyn
char_eowyn.description: Niece of Theoden and sister of Eomer. Trapped in the role assigned to her, she yearns to fight for her people. Her answer to the Witch-king -- 'I am no man' -- is one of the most famous moments in the history of Middle-earth.
char_eowyn.role: Niece of King Theoden, Hidden Warrior

char_faramir.name: Faramir
char_faramir.description: Younger son of Denethor II and brother of Boromir. Where Boromir sought power to save Gondor, Faramir seeks wisdom. His meeting with Frodo in Ithilien is a test of his virtue: the Ring is within reach, and he chooses not to take it.
char_faramir.role: Captain of the Rangers of Ithilien

char_treebeard.name: Treebeard
char_treebeard.description: The oldest Ent of Middle-earth, shepherd of the trees of Fangorn since the First Ages. Ents are creatures of deliberate slowness -- they never speak of anything hastily. But when Treebeard understands the scale of the devastation wrought by Isengard, he summons the Entmoot and leads the Ents to war.
char_treebeard.role: Shepherd of Trees, Eldest of the Ents

char_denethor.name: Denethor II
char_denethor.description: Twenty-sixth Steward of Gondor, father of Boromir and Faramir. Once a man of great will and piercing intelligence. But his secret use of the Palantir of Minas Tirith exposed him to Sauron's influence, who showed him visions of inescapable defeat. Consumed by grief over Boromir and growing despair, he refuses to recognize Aragorn as king and chooses to burn alive with his wounded son Faramir rather than see Gondor fall.

char_witch_king.name: The Witch-king of Angmar
char_witch_king.description: The most powerful of the Nine Nazgul -- former human kings corrupted by Sauron's Rings of Power. He commands the armies of Mordor at the siege of Minas Tirith. The prophecy of Earnur declares that no man can kill him. Eowyn and Merry defy this prophecy on the Pelennor.
char_witch_king.role: Lord of the Nazgul, Lieutenant of Sauron

char_shelob.name: Shelob
char_shelob.description: A colossal and ancient spider, last descendant of Ungoliant who devoured the Trees of Valinor. She has lived in the tunnels of Cirith Ungol for millennia, devouring all who pass -- Orcs, Elves, Men. Gollum knows her and guides Frodo to her as an offering, hoping to recover the Ring from the corpse.

char_grima.name: Grima Wormtongue
char_grima.description: Former counselor to King Theoden, turned by Saruman. He dripped poison and doubt into the king's mind, weakening him so that Rohan could not resist Isengard. Banished by Gandalf at Edoras, he joins Saruman at Orthanc. It is he who throws the Palantir from the window. At the Scouring of the Shire, he kills Saruman before being struck down himself.
char_grima.role: Corrupted counselor of Theoden, Agent of Saruman

char_mouth_sauron.name: The Mouth of Sauron
char_mouth_sauron.description: An ancient Man, corrupted by Sauron's service since the end of the Second Age. He has forgotten his own name. He is sent to parley with Aragorn and Gandalf before the Black Gate, brandishing Frodo's mithril coat and Sting -- suggesting the Ring-bearer has been captured. An attempt to break the morale of the armies of the West.
char_mouth_sauron.role: Ambassador of Sauron at the Black Gate

loc_shire.name: The Shire
loc_shire.description: A verdant agricultural territory in Eriador, inhabited exclusively by Hobbits. The Shire deliberately ignores the rest of the world -- both its strength (preservation of innocence) and its weakness. Frodo's departure marks the end of this golden age.

loc_bree.name: Bree
loc_bree.description: One of the last inhabited towns of Eriador, at the crossroads of two important roads. Bree is rare: it hosts both Men and Hobbits. The Prancing Pony inn is its social heart -- and an information relay for the Rangers.

loc_barrowdowns.name: The Barrow-downs
loc_barrowdowns.description: Hills dotted with ancient barrows, former burial sites of the kings of Arnor. Evil spirits -- Barrow-wights -- were sent there by the Witch-king to haunt the tombs. A place of extreme danger for lost travelers.

loc_weathertop.name: Weathertop
loc_weathertop.description: An isolated summit bearing the ruins of an ancient watchtower of the Kingdom of Arnor. It once housed one of the Palantiri. A strategic location overlooking the surrounding plains -- and thus a gathering point for the Nazgul who watch the roads.

loc_ford.name: Ford of Bruinen
loc_ford.description: The ford on the river Bruinen (Loudwater) that marks the border of Rivendell's protected lands. Elrond can command the waters of the Bruinen. This power was used to create the flood that swept away the Nazgul during Frodo's flight.

loc_rivendell.name: Rivendell
loc_rivendell.description: Founded by Elrond at the end of the Second Age. Nestled in a secret valley of Eriador, protected by the waters of the Bruinen and the power of Vilya. Rivendell is a haven of peace, knowledge and healing. It is here that the Council that decides the fate of the Ring is held.

loc_isengard.name: Isengard
loc_isengard.description: An ancient fortress of the kings of Gondor, entrusted to Saruman's care. He turned it into an industrial and military center, felling forests to fuel his forges. The tower of Orthanc is its heart -- an indestructible black monolith where Gandalf was imprisoned.

loc_caradhras.name: Caradhras Pass
loc_caradhras.description: One of the three passes of the Misty Mountains allowing passage to the East. Caradhras -- the Red Mountain -- is reputed for its malevolent character. During the Fellowship's attempt to cross, an extraordinary snowstorm blocked the path.

loc_moria.name: Mines of Moria
loc_moria.description: Khazad-dum -- the greatest and oldest of the Dwarven cities, carved into the Misty Mountains. Abandoned after the Dwarves accidentally released the Balrog (Durin's Bane) by digging too deep. The mines remain overwhelmingly grand, even overrun by darkness.

loc_lothlorien.name: Lothlorien
loc_lothlorien.description: The Golden Forest, last great Elven domain of Middle-earth. Its Mallorn trees with golden leaves and flets (platforms) high in the canopy create a world outside of time. The power of Nenya protects it from Sauron. Frodo sees in Galadriel's Mirror the possible futures.

loc_parthgalen.name: Parth Galen -- Amon Hen
loc_parthgalen.description: A lawn on the western shore of the Great River (Anduin), at the foot of the Falls of Rauros. Amon Hen (Hill of Sight) overlooks the site. It is here that the Fellowship breaks: Boromir succumbs to the Ring, Frodo flees alone, Merry and Pippin are captured by the Uruk-hai.

loc_mordor.name: Mordor -- Mount Doom
loc_mordor.description: Black lands to the east of the Mountains of Shadow. At the heart of Mordor stands Orodruin, Mount Doom, whose fires allowed Sauron to forge the One Ring in the Second Age. Final destination of the Quest.

loc_emyn_muil.name: Emyn Muil
loc_emyn_muil.description: A labyrinth of rocky hills and cliffs on the eastern bank of the Anduin, south of the Falls of Rauros. Terrain of extreme hostility -- slippery rocks, hidden precipices, impossible orientations. It is here that Frodo and Sam capture Gollum, who has been following them since Lothlorien.

loc_dead_marshes.name: The Dead Marshes
loc_dead_marshes.description: A vast marshy area east of the Emyn Muil, formerly the battlefield of Dagorlad where the armies of the Free Peoples fought Sauron. The faces of the dead from both sides still float beneath the black waters -- illusions or real souls, none can say. To look is mortally dangerous.
inhabitants: Spirits of the dead of Dagorlad

loc_fangorn.name: Fangorn Forest
loc_fangorn.description: The oldest forest of Middle-earth, remnant of the age when trees covered the entire world. Home to trees that see and sometimes act. It is here that Merry and Pippin, fleeing the Uruk-hai, meet Treebeard. It is also here that Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli find Gandalf, returned as the White.

loc_edoras.name: Edoras
loc_edoras.description: Capital of Rohan, built on an isolated hill in the heart of the plains. The great hall of Meduseld (the Golden Hall) is its heart. When Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli arrive, Theoden is a broken old man under the influence of Grima Wormtongue. The liberation of Theoden marks the awakening of all Rohan.

loc_helms_deep.name: Helm's Deep
loc_helms_deep.description: Fortress of Rohan set into a rocky gorge -- reputed impregnable for centuries. On the night of the Battle of Helm's Deep, ten thousand Uruk-hai of Saruman besiege it. Gandalf arrives at dawn with Eomer and his riders to turn the tide of battle.

loc_ithilien.name: Ithilien
loc_ithilien.description: Eastern region of Gondor, long abandoned under pressure from Mordor but patrolled by Faramir's Rangers. Despite the war, it is a land of wild beauty -- clear springs, fragrant herbs, ruins of a thousand-year civilization. It is here that Faramir captures Frodo and Sam.
keyPlaces: The Window on the West (Henneth Annun)

loc_minas_tirith.name: Minas Tirith -- the White City
loc_minas_tirith.description: Capital of Gondor, built in seven circles of white stone against the flank of Mindolluin. The White Tower of Ecthelion dominates the seventh circle. Last bulwark against Mordor. The siege of Minas Tirith is one of the most critical moments of the War of the Ring -- the city holds thanks to Gandalf and the riders of Rohan.

loc_pelennor.name: Pelennor Fields
loc_pelennor.description: A vast grassy plain between Minas Tirith and the Anduin. This is where the greatest battle of the War of the Ring takes place. The charge of the Rohirrim at dawn, the death of Theoden, Eowyn's combat against the Witch-king, and Aragorn's arrival with the black ships turn the tide of war.

loc_cirith_ungol.name: Cirith Ungol
loc_cirith_ungol.description: Pass in the Ephel Duath (Mountains of Shadow), a secret way into Mordor. Shelob's lair overlooks the stairway. An Orc tower guards the pass. This is the path Gollum suggests to Frodo -- knowing Shelob awaits. Sam must infiltrate the tower alone to rescue the captured Frodo.

loc_mount_doom.name: Orodruin -- Mount Doom
loc_mount_doom.description: Active volcano at the heart of Mordor, where Sauron forged the One Ring in the Second Age. The Cracks of Doom (Sammath Naur), on the mountainside, are the only place where the Ring can be destroyed. Final destination of the entire Quest.

loc_paths_dead.name: The Paths of the Dead
loc_paths_dead.description: An underground passage beneath the White Mountains, haunted by the spectres of the Men of the Mountains who had sworn allegiance to Isildur and then betrayed him. Cursed to find no rest until their oath was honored. Aragorn, heir of Isildur, summons them and offers them a chance to redeem their betrayal.

loc_minas_morgul.name: Minas Morgul
loc_minas_morgul.description: Formerly Minas Ithil, Tower of the Moon, an outpost of Gondor. Captured by the Nazgul, it became a place of terror -- greenish light, poisoned air, dead bridge. It is from here that the Witch-king's army marches to besiege Minas Tirith. Frodo and Sam bypass it to reach the stairs of Cirith Ungol.

loc_grey_havens.name: The Grey Havens
loc_grey_havens.description: Last Elven ports of Middle-earth, in the Gulf of Lhun west of Eriador. From here the Elves -- and the Ring-bearers invited by the Valar -- take ship to Valinor, the Undying Lands. Frodo, Gandalf, Bilbo, Galadriel and Elrond embark here. The last farewell.

obj_one_ring.name: The One Ring
obj_one_ring.description: Forged by Sauron in the Second Age to dominate the bearers of the other Rings of Power. It contains the greater part of Sauron's life-force. The Ring corrupts every bearer by awakening their deepest desires and amplifying their will to dominate.
obj_one_ring.inscription: 'One Ring to rule them all, One Ring to find them, One Ring to bring them all, and in the darkness bind them.'
obj_one_ring.creator: Sauron
powers: Signal to the Eye of Sauron

obj_anduril.name: Anduril
obj_anduril.description: Reforged from the shards of Narsil, the sword that cut the Ring from Sauron's hand at the end of the Second Age. Anduril -- 'Flame of the West' -- is the symbol of Aragorn's royal legitimacy. It cannot be broken.
obj_anduril.inscription: 'I am Anduril who was Narsil, the sword of Elendil. Let the servants of Sauron fear my edge.'
obj_anduril.creator: Elves of Rivendell (reforged from Narsil)

obj_sting.name: Sting
obj_sting.description: A short Elven sword from the First Age, found by Bilbo in the trolls' cave. Its blade glows electric blue in the presence of Orcs. Bilbo gives it to Frodo before his departure. It will become the symbol of Frodo's resistance.
obj_sting.creator: Elves of Gondolin (First Age)

obj_mithril.name: Mithril coat
obj_mithril.description: Given to Bilbo by Thorin Oakenshield, then passed to Frodo. The coat is made of mithril -- a metal stronger than steel, lighter than leather. It saves Frodo's life in Moria when a Cave-troll's spear would have pierced him.
obj_mithril.creator: Durin's Dwarves

obj_narya.name: Narya -- the Ring of Fire
obj_narya.description: One of the three Elven Rings, bearing a red ruby. Secretly entrusted to Gandalf by Cirdan the Shipwright upon his arrival in Middle-earth. Narya inspires courage and resistance in those who need it -- a power perfectly suited to Gandalf's mission.
obj_narya.creator: Celebrimbor (forged in Eregion)

obj_phial.name: Phial of Galadriel
obj_phial.description: A glass vial containing the light of the Star of Earendil, reflected in Galadriel's Mirror. Given to Frodo before the departure from Lothlorien. Its light is 'a light to you in dark places, when all other lights go out.'
obj_phial.creator: Galadriel

obj_palantir.name: The Palantir
obj_palantir.description: Seeing Stones capable of communicating across great distances. Several existed in Middle-earth. Saruman possessed one at Orthanc -- it is through it that Sauron corrupted him. Gazing into a Palantir without sufficient mental strength is extremely dangerous.
obj_palantir.creator: Noldor of Valinor

obj_lembas.name: Lembas
obj_lembas.description: Elven waybread of extraordinary nutritive value. A single bite suffices to sustain a grown Man for an entire day's march. Light, compact, it keeps for a long time. Given to each member of the Fellowship before departure from Lothlorien. For Frodo and Sam, it will be the only food on the journey through Mordor.
obj_lembas.creator: Elves of Lothlórien (Vanyar recipe)
obj_lembas.currentHolder: The Fellowship of the Ring (gift from Galadriel)

obj_staves.name: Gandalf's Staff
obj_staves.description: Instrument and symbol of Gandalf's Istari power. It can project a blinding light, ignite fire at a distance, or release a blast of magical force. Its destruction by Saruman during the imprisonment at Orthanc is a powerful act of symbolic domination.
obj_staves.creator: Unknown (brought from Valinor?)

obj_horn_helm.name: Horn of Helm Hammerhand
obj_horn_helm.description: Great war horn of Helm's Deep, named after Helm Hammerhand, legendary king of Rohan. Its sound resonates throughout the gorge and terrorizes enemies. Theoden and Aragorn sound the horn at dawn during the final charge -- a moment of absolute bravery.
obj_horn_helm.creator: Rohirrim (forged for Helm Hammerhand)

obj_ent_draught.name: Ent-draught
obj_ent_draught.description: Mysterious draught that Treebeard gives to Merry and Pippin in Fangorn. Drawn from deep springs of the forest, it makes the hobbits grow several inches -- making them the tallest hobbits in the history of the Shire. A symbol of nature's power against Saruman's industry.
obj_ent_draught.creator: Ents of Fangorn

obj_palantir_mt.name: Palantir of Minas Tirith
obj_palantir_mt.description: One of the seven Seeing Stones, secretly kept by the Stewards of Gondor in the White Tower. Denethor II used it to watch the enemy, but Sauron exploited the connection to show him visions of inescapable defeat, driving him to despair and madness.
obj_palantir_mt.creator: Fëanor (Elves of Valinor)

obj_horn_gondor.name: Horn of Gondor
obj_horn_gondor.description: Great war horn of the Stewards of Gondor, carried by Boromir. Split in two at his death at Parth Galen. The pieces are found and brought back to Denethor -- proof of his eldest son's death, which accelerates his descent into despair.
obj_horn_gondor.creator: Gondor (ancestral)

grp_fellowship.name: The Fellowship of the Ring
grp_fellowship.description: Nine companions chosen at Rivendell to bear the Ring to Mount Doom.

grp_hobbits.name: The Hobbits
grp_hobbits.description: A peaceful people of small stature living in the Shire. Discreet, fond of good living, and surprisingly resilient.

grp_istari.name: The Istari
grp_istari.description: An order of five wizards sent by the Valar to help the Free Peoples against Sauron.

grp_elves.name: The Elves
grp_elves.description: Immortal people, firstborn of Iluvatar, whose power wanes with the passing Ages.

grp_dwarves.name: The Dwarves
grp_dwarves.description: A sturdy people forged by Aule, bound to stone and mine. Proud and tenacious.

grp_ringbearers.name: The Keepers of the Rings
grp_ringbearers.description: Bearers of the Three Elven Rings: Narya (Gandalf), Nenya (Galadriel), Vilya (Elrond).

grp_rohirrim.name: The Rohirrim
grp_rohirrim.description: Riders of Rohan, people of the Mark, descendants of Eorl the Young. Lords of the horses of Middle-earth. Their cavalry is the most feared in the West. Faithful allies of Gondor by the Oath of Eorl.

grp_ents.name: The Ents of Fangorn
grp_ents.description: Shepherds of the trees, the most ancient creatures of Middle-earth. The Ents have watched over the forests since the earliest days. Slow to anger but terrifying once roused -- their march on Isengard is one of the decisive turning points of the war.

grp_rangers_ithilien.name: The Rangers of Ithilien
grp_rangers_ithilien.description: A secret company of Gondorian warriors patrolling Ithilien, the last line of defense before Mordor. Commanded by Faramir, they conduct ambushes against Sauron's armies crossing their lands.

grp_gondor.name: Gondor
grp_gondor.description: Last great kingdom of the Men of the West, founded by the exiles of Numenor. Ruled by Stewards in the absence of Kings for nearly a thousand years. Minas Tirith is its capital. Gondor bears the principal weight of the war against Mordor.

grp_army_dead.name: The Army of the Dead
grp_army_dead.description: Spectres of the Men of the Mountains who had sworn allegiance to Isildur and betrayed him. Cursed to find no rest until their oath was honored. Aragorn, heir of Isildur, summons them and offers redemption for their betrayal by fighting at the Pelennor.

evt_001.title: Bilbo's birthday party
evt_001.description: Bilbo Baggins celebrates his one hundred and eleventh birthday in the Shire. Gandalf prepares the fireworks.

evt_002.title: Bilbo vanishes and bequeaths the Ring
evt_002.description: Bilbo uses the Ring to disappear, then leaves it to Frodo on Gandalf's counsel.

evt_003.title: Bilbo departs for Rivendell
evt_003.description: Bilbo leaves the Shire to go to Rivendell, where he will spend his remaining years.

evt_004.title: Gandalf reveals the truth about the Ring
evt_004.description: Gandalf returns to the Shire and explains to Frodo the true nature of the One Ring.

evt_flash_001.title: Sauron forges the One Ring in Mordor
evt_flash_001.description: Gandalf tells Frodo how Sauron, in the Second Age, forged the One Ring in the fires of Orodruin to subjugate the bearers of the Rings of Power. This tale is a flashback embedded within Gandalf's revelation.

evt_005.title: Gandalf leaves to seek information
evt_005.description: Gandalf leaves the Shire to investigate the Ring's history -- heading to Isengard to consult Saruman.

evt_006.title: Frodo and Sam leave the Shire
evt_006.description: Frodo sells Bag End and sets out on the roads with Sam, awaiting Gandalf who does not come.

evt_007.title: Gandalf imprisoned at Orthanc
evt_007.description: Saruman reveals his treachery and imprisons Gandalf atop the tower of Orthanc at Isengard.

evt_008.title: Tom Bombadil rescues the Hobbits
evt_008.description: Tom Bombadil frees the Hobbits from the Barrow-downs and gives them swords.

evt_009.title: Meeting Strider at Bree
evt_009.description: At the Prancing Pony, the Hobbits meet Aragorn, alias Strider, who offers to guide them to Rivendell.

evt_010.title: Frodo wounded at Weathertop
evt_010.description: The Witch-king wounds Frodo with a Morgul-blade on the ruins of Weathertop (Amon Sul).

evt_011.title: Glorfindel escorts Frodo to the Ford
evt_011.description: Glorfindel, lord of Rivendell, appears and escorts the wounded Frodo to the Ford of Bruinen.

evt_012.title: The flood of the Bruinen repels the Riders
evt_012.description: Elrond unleashes the flood of the Bruinen, sweeping away the Black Riders pursuing Frodo.

evt_013.title: Gandalf escapes Isengard
evt_013.description: Gwaihir the Windlord rescues Gandalf from the pinnacle of Orthanc and carries him to Rivendell.

evt_014.title: Frodo healed by Elrond at Rivendell
evt_014.description: Elrond heals Frodo's wound. Frodo is reunited with Bilbo, old and weary.

evt_015.title: The Great Council -- Frodo volunteers as Ring-bearer
evt_015.description: Representatives of the Free Peoples debate the fate of the Ring. Frodo volunteers to destroy it.

evt_flash_002.title: The Last Alliance -- Isildur cuts Sauron's finger
evt_flash_002.description: Elrond tells the Council how the Last Alliance of Elves and Men defeated Sauron, and how Isildur refused to destroy the Ring after victory, yielding to its corruption. This memory has haunted Elrond for three thousand years.

evt_016.title: Formation of the Fellowship of the Ring
evt_016.description: Elrond forms the Fellowship of nine members to accompany Frodo to Mordor.

evt_017.title: Failure at Caradhras Pass
evt_017.description: The Fellowship attempts to cross the Misty Mountains via Caradhras but is driven back by snow and cold.

evt_018.title: Decision to enter Moria
evt_018.description: Gandalf persuades the Fellowship to cross the Mines of Moria to pass beneath the mountains.

evt_019.title: The Fellowship enters Moria
evt_019.description: The Fellowship enters the Mines through the Western Gate, after Gandalf solves the riddle.

evt_020.title: Discovery of Balin's tomb
evt_020.description: The Fellowship finds Balin's burial chamber. Pippin knocks a skeleton into a well -- the Orcs attack.

evt_021.title: Gandalf falls at the Bridge of Khazad-dum
evt_021.description: Gandalf confronts the Balrog on the Bridge of Khazad-dum. He breaks the bridge but is dragged into the abyss.

evt_022.title: Welcomed by Galadriel and Celeborn
evt_022.description: The Fellowship (without Gandalf) arrives at Caras Galadhon. Galadriel reads their hearts.

evt_023.title: Galadriel gives Lembas and the gifts
evt_023.description: Galadriel gives presents to each member: Elven cloaks, Lembas, vials, and the Phial for Frodo.

evt_024.title: Boromir tries to take the Ring
evt_024.description: Boromir, corrupted by the Ring, attempts to seize it from Frodo on Amon Hen.

evt_025.title: Frodo and Sam cross the River alone
evt_025.description: Frodo decides to continue alone toward Mordor. Sam joins him by swimming -- the Fellowship is broken.

evt_026.title: Death of Boromir
evt_026.description: Boromir is mortally wounded defending Merry and Pippin against the Uruk-hai. Aragorn pays him tribute.

evt_t2_01.title: Frodo and Sam capture Gollum
evt_t2_01.description: In the rocks of the Emyn Muil, Frodo and Sam trap Gollum who has been following them since Parth Galen. Frodo makes him swear on the Ring to guide them to Mordor.

evt_t2_02.title: Crossing the Dead Marshes
evt_t2_02.description: Gollum guides Frodo and Sam through the Dead Marshes. Frodo nearly drowns after gazing at the faces of the dead beneath the black water. Nazgul patrol the skies.

evt_t2_03.title: The impasse at the Black Gate
evt_t2_03.description: Frodo and Sam, guided by Gollum, reach the Black Gate of Mordor (Morannon). It is impenetrable. Gollum proposes a secret path -- Cirith Ungol -- which Frodo reluctantly accepts.

evt_t2_04.title: Faramir captures Frodo in Ithilien
evt_t2_04.description: In Ithilien, Faramir's Rangers ambush a column of Haradrim. Faramir spots Frodo and Sam and leads them to Henneth Annun -- the Window on the West.

evt_t2_05.title: Faramir refuses the Ring -- Gollum revealed
evt_t2_05.description: Faramir interrogates Frodo about his mission. He learns of the Ring's existence and chooses not to take it -- unlike Boromir. Gollum is captured then released at Frodo's request.

evt_t2_06.title: Merry and Pippin escape into Fangorn
evt_t2_06.description: During a Rohirrim attack on the Uruk-hai camp, Merry and Pippin seize the chaos to flee into Fangorn Forest, reputed to be malevolent.

evt_t2_07.title: Meeting Treebeard
evt_t2_07.description: In the forest, Merry and Pippin meet Treebeard (Fangorn), the oldest of the Ents. He welcomes them and listens to their account of Saruman's devastation of the trees -- his anger begins to stir.

evt_t2_08.title: The Ents destroy Isengard
evt_t2_08.description: After the Entmoot -- a deliberation lasting several days -- Treebeard leads the Ents against Isengard. Saruman's fortress is destroyed in a single night: walls shattered, forges drowned. The Ents and Huorns devastate Isengard's army.

evt_t2_09.title: Aragorn finds Gandalf the White
evt_t2_09.description: Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli, who were tracking Merry and Pippin's captors, find in Fangorn an old man in white. They first think it is Saruman -- it is Gandalf, returned from death, transformed into the White.

evt_t2_10.title: Theoden under Grima's thrall
evt_t2_10.description: Gandalf, Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli arrive at Edoras. Theoden, aged and broken by years of Grima Wormtongue's influence, rejects their warnings.

evt_t2_11.title: Gandalf frees Theoden -- banishment of Grima
evt_t2_11.description: Gandalf breaks Saruman's hold on Theoden. The king recovers his vigor and judgment. He exiles Grima Wormtongue from Edoras. Theoden prepares Rohan for war.

evt_t2_12.title: Night of the Battle of Helm's Deep
evt_t2_12.description: Ten thousand Uruk-hai of Saruman besiege Helm's Deep. Aragorn leads the defense alongside Theoden. The wall is blown open by an Uruk-hai powder charge. The situation becomes desperate.

evt_t2_13.title: Gandalf and Eomer at dawn -- victory
evt_t2_13.description: At dawn, Gandalf the White arrives with Eomer and an army of Rohirrim riders. The Huorns of Fangorn encircle the surviving Uruk-hai. The battle turns. Rohan is saved.

evt_t2_14.title: Confrontation with Saruman at Orthanc
evt_t2_14.description: Gandalf, Theoden and Aragorn go to Orthanc to parley with Saruman, holed up in his tower. Gandalf strips him of his rank and breaks his staff. Grima throws the Palantir from the tower.

evt_t2_15.title: Pippin looks into the Palantir
evt_t2_15.description: Pippin, irresistibly drawn, seizes the Palantir and looks into it. Sauron sees him and believes he has found the Ring-bearer. Gandalf realizes Sauron will launch his offensive believing the Ring is at Minas Tirith.

evt_t3_01.title: Gandalf and Pippin arrive at Minas Tirith
evt_t3_01.description: Gandalf rides Shadowfax across Gondor with Pippin. They arrive at Minas Tirith -- seven circles of white stone under the shadow of Mordor. Pippin discovers a magnificent city consumed by fear. Gandalf prepares for the siege.

evt_t3_02.title: Denethor interrogates Pippin about Boromir's death
evt_t3_02.description: Denethor receives Gandalf and Pippin in the Throne Room. He questions Pippin about the exact circumstances of Boromir's death. The hobbit, overwhelmed with gratitude and guilt, swears service to Gondor -- becoming a Guard of the Citadel.

evt_t3_03.title: Aragorn takes the Paths of the Dead
evt_t3_03.description: Aragorn chooses the most dangerous and fastest route: crossing the Paths of the Dead beneath the White Mountains. Invoking his right as heir of Isildur, he summons the Army of the Dead to honor their broken oath -- or wander for eternity.

evt_t3_04.title: Siege of Minas Tirith -- Faramir wounded
evt_t3_04.description: The armies of Mordor besiege Minas Tirith. Faramir leads a desperate sortie to defend Osgiliath but is wounded by a Nazgul's poisoned dart. He is brought back unconscious. The battering ram Grond breaks the gates. Gandalf alone faces the Witch-king.

evt_t3_05.title: Denethor's madness -- the pyre
evt_t3_05.description: Convinced all is lost, Denethor attempts to immolate his wounded son Faramir and himself on a pyre in the Tombs of the Kings. Pippin alerts Gandalf. Beregond and Gandalf save Faramir just in time. Denethor throws himself into the flames clutching the Palantir.

evt_t3_06.title: Theoden's charge at dawn on the Pelennor
evt_t3_06.description: Six thousand riders of Rohan arrive at dawn on the Pelennor. Theoden sounds the horn and charges Mordor's army. A moment of pure heroism -- the greatest cavalry charge in Middle-earth's history. But Theoden is unhorsed by the Witch-king and mortally crushed by his horse.
evt_t3_06.chapterTitle: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields

evt_t3_07.title: Eowyn and Merry slay the Witch-king
evt_t3_07.description: The Witch-king looms over the dying Theoden. Eowyn, disguised as Dernhelm, faces him. 'No man can kill me.' -- 'I am no man.' Merry strikes from behind with his Barrow-blade (enchanted against spirits of Evil). Eowyn finishes the Nazgul. The prophecy is fulfilled.
evt_t3_07.chapterTitle: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields

evt_t3_08.title: Aragorn arrives with the Army of the Dead -- victory at the Pelennor
evt_t3_08.description: As the battle seems to turn against the defenders again -- Mumakil from Harad, the Corsair army -- the black ships sail up the Anduin. But it is Aragorn who disembarks, with the Army of the Dead and the Rangers of the South. The Pelennor is won. The Army of the Dead is freed from their curse.
evt_t3_08.chapterTitle: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields

evt_t3_09.title: March to the Black Gate -- diversion for Frodo
evt_t3_09.description: Aragorn leads the remaining army of Gondor and Rohan before the Black Gate of Mordor -- not to conquer, but to divert Sauron's attention from Frodo. A deliberate sacrifice. Seven thousand men against tens of thousands. Gandalf knows everything rests on the Ring-bearer.

evt_t3_10.title: The Mouth of Sauron -- parley
evt_t3_10.description: Sauron's herald emerges from the Black Gate. He brandishes Frodo's mithril coat and Sting -- evidence that the Ring-bearer has been captured. Despair threatens. But Gandalf refuses to negotiate and snatches the relics. Battle begins.

evt_t3_11.title: The Stairs of Cirith Ungol -- the climb toward the trap
evt_t3_11.description: Frodo, Sam and Gollum bypass Minas Morgul whose greenish light radiates malevolence. They climb the interminable stairs -- Straight Stair then Winding Stair. Frodo weakens. Gollum prepares his betrayal in silence. Sam knows something is wrong but cannot prove it.

evt_t3_12.title: Shelob attacks Frodo -- Sam counterattacks with the Phial and Sting
evt_t3_12.description: Gollum leads Frodo into Shelob's tunnel. The spider attacks and poisons Frodo with her stinger. Sam, desperate, raises the Phial of Galadriel -- the light drives Shelob back -- then strikes the creature with Sting. Shelob retreats, wounded. But Frodo lies still.

evt_t3_13.title: Sam takes the Ring -- believes Frodo dead
evt_t3_13.description: Believing Frodo dead, Sam takes the Ring and Sting. He must continue the Quest alone. But the Orcs arrive and carry Frodo away -- Sam realizes he is only asleep from the venom. Frodo is alive, but a prisoner in the tower of Cirith Ungol.

evt_t3_14.title: Sam infiltrates the tower of Cirith Ungol and rescues Frodo
evt_t3_14.description: Sam, wearing the Ring, infiltrates the tower of Cirith Ungol alone. The Orcs have killed each other over Frodo's mithril coat. Sam finds Frodo naked and tortured on the upper floors. He returns the Ring. They disguise themselves as Orcs and escape toward Mordor.

evt_t3_15.title: Crossing the plateau of Gorgoroth
evt_t3_15.description: Frodo and Sam cross the desolate plains of Mordor toward Mount Doom. Water runs out. Food runs out. The Ring weighs heavier and heavier. Sam literally carries Frodo up the last slope. 'I can't carry it for you, but I can carry you.'

evt_t3_16.title: Frodo claims the Ring -- Gollum falls into the fire
evt_t3_16.description: At the edge of the Cracks of Doom, Frodo finally yields to the Ring: 'The Ring is mine.' He puts it on his finger. But Gollum, who has followed them, lunges at him, bites off his finger and the Ring, and falls into the lava -- destroying the One Ring. Frodo's pity for Gollum has saved the world.

evt_t3_17.title: The Ring destroyed -- Sauron falls -- the Eagles
evt_t3_17.description: The Ring is destroyed. Barad-dur collapses. Sauron's army at the Black Gate disintegrates. Mordor crumbles upon itself. Gandalf sends Gwaihir's Eagles to rescue Frodo and Sam on the slopes of the erupting Mountain.

evt_t3_18.title: Aragorn's coronation -- the King has returned
evt_t3_18.description: Aragorn is crowned King Elessar Telcontar of the reunited Gondor and Arnor. Gandalf places the Winged Crown upon his head. Arwen Undomiel arrives -- they wed. The hobbits are honored before the assembled people. The Fourth Age begins.

evt_t3_19.title: The Grey Havens -- Frodo departs for Valinor
evt_t3_19.description: Frodo, too deeply wounded by the burden of the Ring, is granted the right to sail to the Undying Lands with Gandalf, Bilbo, Galadriel and Elrond. At the Grey Havens, Sam bids farewell to his master. The White Ship vanishes over the horizon. Sam goes home: 'Well, I'm back.'

ch1.title: A Long-Expected Party
ch1.summary: The Shire is presented in all its Hobbit tranquility. Bilbo celebrates his 111th birthday and passes the Ring to Frodo. Gandalf watches, uneasy. The peaceful world and the underlying threat are established.

ch2.title: The Shadow of the Past
ch2.summary: Gandalf reveals the true nature of the Ring to Frodo. Sauron is searching for it. Frodo must leave the Shire. The fate of the world rests on a simple hobbit.

ch3.title: The Road to Rivendell
ch3.summary: Frodo hesitates and wavers. The journey to Rivendell is fraught with peril. At Rivendell, the Council of Elrond debates the Ring's future. Frodo volunteers.

ch4.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
ch4.summary: The Fellowship is formed. Aragorn, Frodo's confidant, represents the subplot of hidden kingship. The company heads south then attempts the pass of Caradhras.

ch5.title: Moria
ch5.summary: The Fellowship enters the Mines of Moria. Battle against the Balrog. Gandalf falls into the abyss, sacrificing himself to save the group.

ch6.title: Lorien
ch6.summary: Refuge at Lothlorien. Galadriel tests Frodo and offers him a mirror of visions. Boromir grows ever more corrupted by the Ring. The Fellowship departs on the Anduin.

ch7.title: The Betrayal of Boromir
ch7.summary: Boromir yields to the Ring and attacks Frodo. Frodo flees. The Fellowship is attacked by the Uruk-hai. All seems lost: the mission and the group are in peril.

ch8.title: The Fall of Boromir
ch8.summary: Boromir redeems himself by dying to defend Merry and Pippin. Frodo realizes he must continue alone to protect his friends. He sets out with Sam.

ch9.title: The Departure for Mordor
ch9.summary: Frodo and Sam set out alone toward Mordor. The final image contrasts with the initial tranquility of the Shire: two hobbits walk toward the dark lands, determined.

ch_t2_01.title: The Bearer Alone -- Gollum Captured
ch_t2_01.summary: Frodo and Sam, alone after the breaking, press on through the crags of the Emyn Muil. They capture Gollum who was following them. Frodo gives him a chance -- a new arc of ambiguous trust. Opening image of the second volume: two exhausted hobbits and a tortured guide.

ch_t2_02.title: The Doubtful Guide
ch_t2_02.summary: Gollum guides Frodo and Sam through the Dead Marshes. His Smeagol/Gollum duality asserts itself. Frodo feels pity for him -- Sam mistrusts. The three-way relationship is established as the B-story of the volume.

ch_t2_03.title: Merry, Pippin and the Ents
ch_t2_03.summary: Merry and Pippin find refuge in Fangorn and meet Treebeard. The Ent narrative thread opens in parallel. Two stories unfold simultaneously -- Aragorn/Legolas/Gimli track their lost friends.

ch_t2_04.title: Return of Gandalf the White
ch_t2_04.summary: In Fangorn, Aragorn finds Gandalf -- returned from death, more powerful. The midpoint of the volume: everything changes. A lost ally is recovered, transformed. Hope is reborn. Gandalf reveals the situation is worse than expected -- and time is running out.

ch_t2_05.title: Edoras -- The Awakening of Rohan
ch_t2_05.summary: Arrival at Edoras, healing of Theoden, expulsion of Grima. Rohan awakens for war. Eowyn appears -- subplot of the hidden warrior. Forces gather to defend Helm's Deep.

ch_t2_06.title: The Black Gate and Ithilien
ch_t2_06.summary: Frodo realizes the direct way is impossible. Gollum proposes Cirith Ungol. Sam opposes. Meeting with Faramir -- the Ring is within reach of a man of Gondor, and he chooses not to take it. Contrast with Boromir.

ch_t2_06b.title: The Window on the West
ch_t2_06b.summary: Faramir captures Frodo and Sam in Ithilien. He discovers the Ring's existence and faces the same temptation as his brother Boromir. But where Boromir yielded, Faramir chooses not to take it -- proving a man of quality can resist. Gollum is captured at the forbidden pool, then released out of regard for Frodo.

ch_t2_07.title: The Night of Helm's Deep
ch_t2_07.summary: The Battle of Helm's Deep -- a night without hope. The wall explodes, defenses crumble. Aragorn and Theoden hold off the inevitable. All seems lost. The darkest night of the volume.

ch_t2_08.title: The March of the Ents -- Dawn
ch_t2_08.summary: Double reversal: Gandalf and Eomer arrive at Helm's Deep at dawn and save Rohan. Simultaneously, the Ents destroy Isengard. Saruman is neutralized. The second front of the war turns in favor of the Free Peoples.

ch_t2_09.title: Into the Darkness
ch_t2_09.summary: Confrontation with Saruman at Orthanc -- he is deposed. Pippin looks into the Palantir, partially revealing the Ring to Sauron. Frodo and Sam resume their road toward Cirith Ungol with Gollum. Final image: two hobbits and a tortured creature walk toward absolute darkness.

ch_t3_01.title: Minas Tirith -- the White City
ch_t3_01.summary: Gandalf and Pippin arrive at Minas Tirith. Denethor, the Steward, receives the news of Boromir's death. Pippin swears service to Gondor. The city prepares for the siege. Opening image of the last volume: a white city under a growing black shadow.

ch_t3_02.title: The Stairs of Cirith Ungol
ch_t3_02.summary: Frodo, Sam and Gollum bypass Minas Morgul and climb the interminable stairs toward the pass of Cirith Ungol. The Ring's weight increases. The volume's theme crystallizes: can one accomplish the impossible when the price is the loss of oneself?

ch_t3_03.title: The Paths of the Dead
ch_t3_03.summary: Aragorn leaves Edoras for the shortest and most terrible road. With Legolas and Gimli, he crosses the Dwimorberg and summons the Army of the Dead. In parallel, Merry pledges fealty to Theoden and rides secretly toward Gondor with Eowyn in disguise.

ch_t3_04.title: The Siege of Gondor
ch_t3_04.summary: The siege begins. Faramir is wounded. Grond breaks the gates. Gandalf alone stands against the Witch-king. Denethor, broken by the Palantir, tries to burn Faramir and himself. The volume's midpoint -- the situation is at its darkest.

ch_t3_05.title: The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
ch_t3_05.summary: Dawn brings the Rohirrim. Theoden charges -- and dies heroically. Eowyn and Merry slay the Witch-king. Aragorn arrives by river. The battle is won, but the cost is immense. The military climax of the volume.

ch_t3_06.title: Shelob's Lair
ch_t3_06.summary: Gollum leads Frodo into Shelob's tunnel. The spider poisons Frodo. Sam, alone, uses the Phial and Sting to repel the creature. Believing Frodo dead, he takes the Ring. The Orcs carry Frodo away -- he is alive. All is lost for Sam.

ch_t3_07.title: The Black Gate
ch_t3_07.summary: Double front: Aragorn leads the remaining army before the Black Gate as a diversion. The Mouth of Sauron brandishes Frodo's relics. In parallel, Sam infiltrates the tower of Cirith Ungol and rescues Frodo. The third act begins.

ch_t3_08.title: Mount Doom
ch_t3_08.summary: Frodo and Sam cross Mordor. Sam carries Frodo up the last slopes. At the edge of the Cracks of Doom, Frodo yields to the Ring. Gollum tears it away and falls into the lava. The Ring is destroyed. Sauron collapses. The Eagles rescue the hobbits. The absolute finale.

ch_t3_09.title: The Grey Havens
ch_t3_09.summary: Aragorn is crowned King Elessar. The hobbits return to the Shire. Frodo, too wounded by the burden, is granted passage to the Undying Lands. At the Grey Havens, he bids farewell to Sam, Merry and Pippin. The White Ship vanishes. Sam goes home: 'Well, I'm back.' Final image of the entire trilogy.

plant_001.label: The Ring inherited from Bilbo
plant_001.notes: Bilbo bequeaths the Ring to Frodo at his birthday party. Gandalf reveals its true nature in the following chapter.

plant_002.label: Bilbo's mithril coat
plant_002.notes: Bilbo gives his coat to Frodo at Rivendell. It will save him from an Orc spear in Balin's chamber in Moria.

plant_003.label: Sting's blade glows near Orcs
plant_003.notes: Gandalf explains that Sting glows in the presence of Orcs -- a property established during the journey. Confirmed at the attack on Weathertop.

plant_004.label: The prophecy of Gondor's dreams about Isildur
plant_004.notes: Gandalf mentions Isildur's heir. The Council of Elrond reveals that Aragorn is that heir.

plant_005.label: Boromir's temptation by the Ring
plant_005.notes: At the Council, Boromir proposes using the Ring as a weapon. His growing conviction leads to his attack on Frodo at Amon Hen.

plant_006.label: Galadriel's refusal of the Ring
plant_006.notes: Galadriel refuses the Ring offered by Frodo, choosing to remain herself. This inspires Frodo to depart alone to protect his companions.

plant_007.label: Gandalf and Saruman's secret
plant_007.notes: Gandalf goes to consult Saruman and is imprisoned. At the Council, he reveals the betrayal of the head of the Istari.

plant_008.label: The Phial of Galadriel for the darkness
plant_008.notes: Galadriel gives her Phial to Frodo -- 'a light for you in dark places'. The resolution will come in later volumes.

plant_t2_01.label: Gollum announced by Gandalf in V1, guide in V2
plant_t2_01.notes: Gandalf mentions to Frodo that Gollum had been tracking the Ring for centuries. This shadow-character, planted in chapter 2, becomes the pivotal guide of the entire second volume.

plant_t2_02.label: The Phial of Galadriel -- light in the darkness
plant_t2_02.notes: Given to Frodo 'for dark places when all other lights go out'. The resolution will come in Volume 3 against Shelob in Cirith Ungol.

plant_t2_03.label: Saruman's hold on Theoden
plant_t2_03.notes: Gandalf's imprisonment at Isengard (V1) reveals that Saruman has agents everywhere. His hold on Theoden is a direct consequence of this corruption -- resolved when Gandalf frees the king.

plant_t2_04.label: The Palantir of Orthanc -- Sauron's vision
plant_t2_04.notes: The Seeing Stone is planted from Gandalf's imprisonment at Orthanc. Its revelation in V2 (Pippin looks, Sauron sees) accelerates the war -- and sets up the Minas Tirith arc in V3.

plant_t2_05.label: Frodo's pity for Gollum
plant_t2_05.notes: Frodo chooses to spare Gollum and trust him against Sam's advice. This pity, incomprehensible to Sam, will prove of capital importance at Mount Doom (V3). Open seed.

plant_t3_01.label: The Phial of Galadriel -- light against Shelob
plant_t3_01.notes: Galadriel gives the Phial to Frodo 'for dark places when all other lights go out'. This is exactly what happens in Shelob's lair: Sam raises the Phial, and the light of Earendil repels the spider. Planted in V1, resolved in V3.

plant_t3_02.label: Frodo's pity for Gollum -- salvation at Mount Doom
plant_t3_02.notes: Frodo chooses to spare Gollum and trust him, against Sam's advice. This pity, incomprehensible in V2, saves the world in V3: it is Gollum who, by tearing the Ring from Frodo, inadvertently destroys it by falling into the lava. Without the pity, no destruction of the Ring.

plant_t3_03.label: Merry's Barrow-blade -- death of the Witch-king
plant_t3_03.notes: Tom Bombadil saves the hobbits from the Barrow-downs and gives them swords forged against the Witch-king of Angmar long ago. Merry's is precisely enchanted to break the bond between the Nazgul and the physical world -- without it, Eowyn's blow would not have sufficed. A plant from chapter 3 of V1 resolved in chapter 24 of V3.

plant_t3_04.label: Aragorn's destiny -- the King is crowned
plant_t3_04.notes: Since the Council of Elrond (V1 ch4), Aragorn's destiny as heir of Isildur and future king of Gondor is established. The reforged sword (Anduril), the Paths of the Dead, the Battle of the Pelennor -- everything converges toward the coronation in V3 ch28. The longest arc of the trilogy.

plant_t3_05.label: Denethor's Palantir -- the Steward's madness
plant_t3_05.notes: From Gandalf's arrival, Denethor's behavior betrays knowledge he should not have -- fruit of his secret use of the Palantir. This plant resolves when Denethor throws himself into the flames clutching the Stone, finally revealing the source of his despair.

plant_t3_06.label: Eowyn disguised as Dernhelm -- the prophecy fulfilled
plant_t3_06.notes: Eowyn rides secretly with the Rohirrim, disguised as a rider named Dernhelm, taking Merry with her. At the Pelennor, she reveals her identity to the Witch-king who declares no man can kill him: 'I am no man.' The prophecy of Glorfindel is fulfilled.

thr_quest.name: The Quest of the Ring
thr_quest.description: Main thread: destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom before Sauron recovers it.

thr_aragorn.name: Aragorn's Destiny
thr_aragorn.description: The gradual revelation of Aragorn's royal identity -- heir of Isildur -- and his difficult acceptance of his heritage.

thr_boromir.name: The Corruption of Boromir
thr_boromir.description: Boromir's growing temptation by the Ring, his moral fall and his final heroic redemption.

thr_rohan.name: The Awakening of Rohan
thr_rohan.description: The liberation of Theoden, the mustering of Rohan and the defense of Helm's Deep -- a horse-people rising against Saruman's tide.

thr_ents.name: The March of the Ents
thr_ents.description: Treebeard and the Ents' slow anger at Fangorn's destruction by Isengard, culminating in the destruction of Saruman's fortress.

thr_gollum.name: The Duality of Smeagol
thr_gollum.description: The inner war between Smeagol (pity, fragile loyalty) and Gollum (obsession, betrayal) -- and the question of whether Frodo's pity is wisdom or naivety.

thr_gondor.name: The Defense of Gondor
thr_gondor.description: The siege of Minas Tirith, Denethor's madness, Faramir's wounding. Gandalf and Pippin at the heart of the besieged city. Culmination: the Gate broken by Grond and Gandalf alone against the Witch-king.

thr_shelob.name: Shelob's Lair
thr_shelob.description: Gollum's betrayal takes shape: he leads Frodo into Shelob's trap. Sam alone must save his master. The thread that crystallizes Sam's transformation from simple gardener to hero.

thr_return.name: The Return of the King
thr_return.description: Aragorn's arc reaches its resolution: the Paths of the Dead, the Pelennor, the coronation. In parallel, the hobbits' return to the Shire and Frodo's departure at the Grey Havens. The end of an age, the beginning of another.

inc_001.title: Gandalf imprisoned at Isengard: before or after the Council?
inc_001.explanation: Gandalf is listed as a visitor of Isengard and is imprisoned there by Saruman, but no chronological data specifies whether this capture occurred before or after the formation of the Fellowship at Rivendell. His simultaneous presence as the Fellowship's guide and Orthanc's prisoner creates an unresolved temporal ambiguity.

inc_002.title: Thorin Oakenshield mentioned but absent from the database
inc_002.explanation: The Mithril coat states it was 'given to Bilbo by Thorin Oakenshield', but Thorin does not exist as an entity in the database. This crucial character is cited in an object's description without being referenceable, making the chain of possession incomplete.

inc_003.title: Gandalf listed as holder of Lembas despite his absence from Lothlorien
inc_003.explanation: Lembas lists Gandalf among its holders, but this Elven bread was given by Galadriel at Lothlorien after the crossing of Moria. Gandalf fell at the Bridge of Khazad-dum before the Fellowship reached Lothlorien -- he therefore cannot be among the Lembas holders.

inc_004.title: Glorfindel absent from Rivendell despite his role as Elf-lord
inc_004.explanation: Glorfindel is listed as a visitor of the Ford of Bruinen and his origin is 'Rivendell -- Imladris', but he does not appear in Rivendell's visitedBy list. An Elf-lord of Rivendell who appears at the Ford with no trace of his presence in the Elven city he is supposed to protect constitutes a traceability inconsistency.

inc_005.title: Anduril forged by 'Elves of Rivendell' with no associated entity
inc_005.explanation: Anduril's creator is 'Elves of Rivendell (reforge of Narsil)', but this collective entity is not referenced. Elrond, Lord of Rivendell and bearer of Vilya, would be the logical master smith of this reforging -- yet no direct link is established between him and the sword in the database.

inc_006.title: Tom Bombadil from an unreferenced location
inc_006.explanation: Tom Bombadil's origin is 'Old Forest' and his affiliation is 'Old Forest (independent)', but this place does not exist as a location entity in the database. His domain -- the Barrow-downs -- is present, but the Old Forest itself remains an orphan reference.

inc_007.title: Boromir affiliated with 'Gondor': location absent from database
inc_007.explanation: Boromir has the affiliation 'Gondor', but Gondor exists neither as a location nor as an entity in the database. His origin 'Minas Tirith -- Gondor' suggests that Gondor should be a referenced location. This orphan affiliation prevents creating any graphical link to his native faction.

inc_008.title: Gandalf's Staff: unknown creator and place of creation
inc_008.explanation: Gandalf's Staff indicates 'Unknown (brought from Valinor?)' as creator and 'Unknown' as place of creation. Yet Valinor is mentioned as Gandalf's own origin -- minimal consistency would require his staff be associated with the same origin, or that Valinor be added as a location entity.

inc_t2_01.title: Eomer banished then at Helm's Deep -- fuzzy chronology
inc_t2_01.explanation: Eomer is banished from Edoras by Theoden under Grima's influence for disobedience. Yet a few events later, he arrives at dawn at Helm's Deep with his army of riders. The exact duration and conditions of his banishment -- was he free to fight regardless? -- are not specified, creating a status inconsistency.

inc_t2_02.title: Grima Wormtongue absent from the database as an entity
inc_t2_02.explanation: Grima Wormtongue is the pivot of the Rohan sequence -- his sorcery on Theoden is the starting point of the entire Edoras narrative thread. He is mentioned in several events but does not exist as a character entity in the database. His chain of actions (thrall, banishment, throwing the Palantir) therefore cannot be traced.

inc_t2_03.title: The Palantir -- who threw it, who holds it?
inc_t2_03.explanation: The Palantir is listed as belonging to Saruman, current holder. Yet it is Grima (unreferenced) who throws it from the tower of Orthanc. Pippin picks it up. The actual chain of possession (Saruman, Grima, Pippin, Gandalf) is not reflected in the database.

inc_t2_04.title: Faramir affiliated with 'Gondor' -- location absent from database
inc_t2_04.explanation: Like his brother Boromir, Faramir carries the affiliation 'Gondor', but Gondor does not exist as a location entity in the database. Minas Tirith is not referenced either. The Gondor affiliation of both of Denethor's sons thus remains an orphan affiliation with no target entity.

inc_t3_01.title: Denethor 'sees' through the Palantir but not the truth
inc_t3_01.explanation: The Palantiri show the truth -- but Sauron controlled what Denethor could see, showing him only visions of defeat and overwhelming power. The Palantir does not lie, but its user can be manipulated by a stronger mind. The Stone's 'omnipotence' is therefore conditional, which the narrative does not always make explicit.

inc_t3_02.title: The Army of the Dead vanishes after the Pelennor -- why not use them against Mordor?
inc_t3_02.explanation: Aragorn releases the Army of the Dead from their oath as soon as the Pelennor is won, even though they could have marched on Mordor and crushed Sauron. Explanation: the oath was tied to a specific act (defending Gondor), and keeping the dead beyond that would have been an act of domination -- contrary to Aragorn's nature. Nevertheless, the narrative does not explicitly detail this limitation.

inc_t3_03.title: The mithril coat taken at Cirith Ungol then shown at the Black Gate
inc_t3_03.explanation: The Orcs take the mithril coat from Frodo in the tower of Cirith Ungol. The Mouth of Sauron brandishes it at the Black Gate -- he recovered it. But how did an object taken by an Orc from an isolated garrison reach Barad-dur and then the Gate so quickly? The object's tracking in the database is discontinuous.

inc_t3_04.title: The Eagles at Mount Doom -- why not sooner?
inc_t3_04.explanation: Gwaihir's Eagles rescue Frodo and Sam after the Ring's destruction. The classic question: why not fly directly to Mordor from the start? The Eagles are sovereign beings, not mounts. The winged Nazgul control the sky. The Ring would have corrupted an Eagle. But the text does not explicitly provide these explanations -- it is a recurring point of debate among readers.

char_frodo_ordinary_world.summary: Frodo leads a peaceful life in the Shire, heir to Bilbo, with no heroic ambitions.

char_frodo_call_to_adventure.summary: Gandalf reveals the truth about the One Ring -- Frodo must carry it far from the Shire.

char_frodo_refusal.summary: Frodo tries to give the Ring to Gandalf, seeking to flee the responsibility.

char_frodo_mentor.summary: Gandalf guides and protects Frodo, reveals the Ring's history and shows him the way.

char_frodo_threshold.summary: Frodo leaves the Shire with Sam. The meeting with Aragorn seals his commitment to the adventure.

char_frodo_tests.summary: Weathertop, the Witch-king's wound, the flight to the Ford -- Frodo learns the price of courage.

char_frodo_inmost_cave.summary: Moria: Frodo enters absolute darkness, confronted with the ancient terror of the Balrog.

char_frodo_ordeal.summary: Gandalf falls at the Bridge of Khazad-dum. The Fellowship loses its guide -- Frodo must carry on alone.

char_frodo_reward.summary: Lothlorien: rest, Galadriel's gifts, the Phial of light -- Frodo receives the tools of his victory.

char_frodo_road_back.summary: Frodo decides to go alone toward Mordor, refusing to put his companions in danger.

char_frodo_resurrection.summary: The confrontation with Boromir reveals the Ring's corruption -- Frodo must die to his former life.

char_frodo_return_with_elixir.summary: Frodo and Sam cross the river. The elixir is not yet won -- the true ordeal begins.

char_gandalf_ordinary_world.summary: Gandalf the Grey has wandered Middle-earth for centuries -- a discreet guide, fireworks and wisdom. An Istari among the Free Peoples, tireless watchman.

char_gandalf_call_to_adventure.summary: Gandalf identifies Bilbo's ring as the One Ring. Sauron's threat is confirmed -- he must act now or all will be lost.

char_gandalf_refusal.summary: Frodo offers him the Ring. Gandalf refuses in terror: 'Do not tempt me!' -- he knows such power would corrupt him despite his good intentions.

char_gandalf_mentor.summary: At the Council of Elrond, Gandalf orchestrates the formation of the Fellowship. He does not merely guide -- he gives a common purpose to nine walkers whom everything separates.

char_gandalf_threshold.summary: Gandalf leads the Fellowship out of Rivendell. The choice of Moria, against all counsel, seals his commitment: he will bear the consequences.

char_gandalf_tests.summary: Caradhras repels the Fellowship. The doors of Moria, the approaching Balrog's darkness -- Gandalf navigates between dangers while shielding the group.

char_gandalf_inmost_cave.summary: The Bridge of Khazad-dum. Gandalf faces the Balrog of Morgoth -- a Maiar against a Maiar. 'You shall not pass!'

char_gandalf_ordeal.summary: Gandalf falls with the Balrog into the depths of Khazad-dum. Death of Gandalf the Grey -- sacrifice to save the Fellowship.

char_gandalf_reward.summary: Sent back by the Valar, Gandalf returns as Gandalf the White -- more powerful, wiser, invested with new authority to complete his mission.

char_gandalf_road_back.summary: Gandalf frees Theoden from Saruman's thrall, rallies Rohan and orchestrates the defense of Helm's Deep. The counteroffensive begins.

char_gandalf_resurrection.summary: Before the Black Gate, Gandalf leads the army of the West in a suicidal diversion. He knows everything rests on Frodo -- and accepts dying a second time if he must.

char_gandalf_return_with_elixir.summary: The Ring destroyed, Sauron vanquished. Gandalf crowns Aragorn, accompanies the Hobbits home, then embarks at the Grey Havens -- his mission in Middle-earth is complete.

char_aragorn_ordinary_world.summary: Aragorn at Parth Galen after Boromir's death -- a guide without a Fellowship, without a clear heading.

char_aragorn_call_to_adventure.summary: The return of Gandalf the White redefines the mission: go to Edoras, rally Rohan.

char_aragorn_refusal.summary: Aragorn doubts his heritage: the shadow of Isildur weighs on him. Can he claim the throne without repeating his ancestor's weakness?

char_aragorn_mentor.summary: Gandalf the White -- wiser, more powerful -- resumes his role as mentor and strategist.

char_aragorn_threshold.summary: Edoras: Aragorn enters the hall of a corrupted king, with no certainty of success.

char_aragorn_tests.summary: Free Theoden, convince the Rohirrim, prepare for a battle with no real hope.

char_aragorn_inmost_cave.summary: Helm's Deep: a besieged fortress, a night with no way out -- the cave of despair.

char_aragorn_ordeal.summary: The wall explodes, the enemy enters -- Aragorn must choose between surviving and sacrificing.

char_aragorn_reward.summary: Dawn and Gandalf -- the unexpected victory at Helm's Deep. The resistance held.

char_aragorn_road_back.summary: March to the devastated Isengard -- the war is not over, but one front is closed.

char_aragorn_resurrection.summary: Facing Saruman in his tower: Aragorn resists the enchanting voice -- identity proven.

char_aragorn_return_with_elixir.summary: Aragorn sets out toward the war to come -- strengthened, recognized, the king-in-waiting asserts himself.

char_sam_ordinary_world.summary: Sam follows Frodo toward Mordor -- a faithful gardener with no heroic pretension. His strength comes from simple loyalty and his love for the Shire.

char_sam_call_to_adventure.summary: The Stairs of Cirith Ungol -- the road becomes lethal. Sam understands this quest may have no return.

char_sam_refusal.summary: Sam wants to convince Frodo not to follow Gollum into the tunnel. His instinct screams trap, but Frodo will not listen.

char_sam_mentor.summary: The memory of Gandalf and the light of the Phial: 'There's some good in this world, Mr. Frodo, and it's worth fighting for.'

char_sam_threshold.summary: Sam takes the Ring believing Frodo dead -- he becomes a Ring-bearer. Crossing the threshold: from aide to hero.

char_sam_tests.summary: Sam infiltrates the tower of Cirith Ungol alone -- fights Orcs, finds Frodo naked and tortured. The loneliest ordeal.

char_sam_inmost_cave.summary: The plain of Gorgoroth -- march toward Mount Doom. No water, no food. Sam carries Frodo up the last slopes.

char_sam_ordeal.summary: Frodo claims the Ring at the edge of the Cracks of Doom. The ultimate nightmare for Sam -- his master has yielded.

char_sam_reward.summary: Gollum falls with the Ring -- the Ring is destroyed. The Quest is accomplished. Sam and Frodo are saved by the Eagles.

char_sam_road_back.summary: Return to the Shire -- but the world has changed. Sam must learn to live after the adventure.

char_sam_resurrection.summary: Sam faces the Scouring of the Shire -- he proves he has become a leader, not just a follower.

char_sam_return_with_elixir.summary: Sam plants Galadriel's mallorn at Hobbiton, marries Rosie, founds his family and becomes Mayor of the Shire. The quiet hero who saved the world goes home: 'Well, I'm back.'
